question.value: Why is the star formation rate linearly proportional to the dense molecular gas mass (the Gao-Solomon relation), and can this proportionality be explained by deterministic relationships between the gravitationally bound gas mass, the mass of the most massive core, the mass of the most massive star, and the star formation rate?

evidence.quote: One of the most profound empirical laws of star formation is the Gao-Solomon relation, a linear correlation between the star formation rate (SFR) and the dense molecular gas mass. It is puzzling how the complicated physics in star-formation results in this surprisingly simple proportionality.

In this work, we attempt to explain the Gao-Solomon relation with an alternative picture. Our main hypothesis is that the mass of the most massive core (M_core^max) in a molecular cloud is determined by the mass of the parent gravitational bound gas reservoir (M_gas^bound).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.01355.L

claims.hypothesis: The mass of the most massive core (M_core^max) in a molecular cloud is determined by the mass of the parent gravitationally bound gas reservoir (M_gas^bound).
claims.experiment: Extracted cores at a matched 0.03 pc spatial resolution from Herschel HGBS N_H2 maps for 11 nearby clouds and ALMA-IMF 1.3 mm continuum maps for 12 distant massive clouds, and measured M_gas^bound from the power-law tail of each cloud's Herschel N-PDF.
claims.result: Found log(M_core^max/M_sun) = 0.506 log(M_gas^bound/M_sun) - 0.32 with Spearman r = 0.83 (p = 7.8e-7), tightening to slope 0.55 and r = 0.96 when excluding 4 distant clouds affected by missing flux.
claims.finding: There is a tight, significant power-law correlation between M_core^max and M_gas^bound across 10^2 to 10^5 M_sun.

evidence.quote: Our main hypothesis is that the mass of the most massive core (M_core^max) in a molecular cloud is determined by the mass of the parent gravitational bound gas reservoir (M_gas^bound).

evidence.loc: 3.3. Mass correlation between most massive core and gravitationally bound gas
evidence.quote: with a Spearman coefficient of 0.83 and a p-value of 7.8

claims.hypothesis: The linear Gao-Solomon relation (SFR proportional to dense gas mass) is a consequence of combining three non-trivial relations: SFR vs. m_star^max (from optimal IMF sampling), m_star^max vs. M_core^max, and M_core^max vs. M_gas^bound.
claims.experiment: Combined the observed M_core^max-M_gas^bound scaling (slope 0.506) with a constant 30% core-to-star efficiency (m_star^max = 0.3 M_core^max) and the theoretical optimal IMF sampling relation log(SFR) = 2.04 log(m_star^max) - 5.80 from Yan et al. (2017) to compute SFR^theory and compare it to the rescaled Gao-Solomon relation and observational SFRs.
claims.result: SFR^theory scales as (M_gas^bound)^1.03 across all clouds (or 1.11 +/- 0.10 excluding outliers) and aligns well with the Lada et al. (2012) rescaled Gao-Solomon relation; SFR^theory also agrees closely with YSO-based SFR^observation in nearby clouds, though distant clouds show large scatter.
claims.finding: The empirical M_core^max-M_gas^bound relation, when paired with a 30% star formation efficiency and optimal IMF sampling, reproduces the linear proportionality of the Gao-Solomon relation.

claims.hypothesis: Core formation in molecular clouds does not stochastically (randomly) sample a universal Core Mass Function (CMF), but instead follows a deterministic/optimal sampling process.
claims.experiment: Performed Monte Carlo simulations randomly drawing n(M > 3 M_sun) cores from power-law CMFs (Gamma = -1.00 and -1.35) for the nearby HGBS clouds (5000 realizations per cloud, and 10^6 iterations for Taurus and Perseus combined) and compared the mock M_core^max distributions to observations.
claims.result: Random CMF sampling yields a much larger scatter (mean standard deviation 0.121–0.139 dex vs. 0.077 dex observed) and systematically overpredicts M_core^max; for Taurus and Perseus combined (172 cores > 3 M_sun), the probability of having no core > 41.1 M_sun under random sampling is <= 8.1 x 10^-3 (>99.1% confidence rejection).
claims.finding: Observed M_core^max values are inconsistent with random sampling of the CMF, supporting a deterministic cluster/core formation picture.

why_this_data.value: Combined Herschel HGBS and Hi-GAL data with ALMA-IMF 1.3 mm data to cover both nearby low-mass clouds and distant massive protoclusters across three orders of magnitude in bound gas mass (10^2 to 10^5 M_sun), using ALMA-IMF to resolve dense cores at 2–5.5 kpc.

evidence.quote: and Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations on a sample of nearby and distant star-forming molecular clouds.
to be located at distances between 2 and 5.5 kpc for both resolving core-like structures and covering the entire extent of the parsec-size clouds with ALMA mosaics

why_this_method.value: Smoothed all maps to a common 0.03 pc spatial resolution and used the same SExtractor procedure for consistent core extraction across nearby and distant clouds; used MLE + MCMC on unbinned N-PDFs to avoid binning pitfalls; substituted M_gas^bound for M_gas^dense to avoid HCN excitation ambiguities.

evidence.quote: We emphasize that in this study, all the core-like structures in nearby and distant molecular clouds were extracted using the same procedure and from maps with the same spatial resolution of 0.03 pc for consistency.
This approach avoids the need to pre-bin the observed column density distributions, thereby circumventing the potential pitfalls associated with binning (Virkar & Clauset 2012).
Here, we are pushing forward to use M_gas^bound to substitute the concept of M_gas^dense referred in the Gao-Solomon relation (Gao & Solomon 2004).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Stochastic picture (random sampling of a universal IMF/CMF explained via the central limit theorem) — rejected on sub-galactic/cloud scales because observed M_core^max-M_gas^bound and m_star^max-m_star^cluster relations are too tight and systematically offset compared to random sampling.

evidence.quote: For example, one might consider that each unit of M_gas^dense in the molecular clouds provides an equal chance to randomly sample a universal stellar initial mass function (IMF) through an identical process (hereafter referred to as the stochastic picture).

evidence.loc: 4.2. Indication of a non-stochastic sampling of core mass
evidence.quote: In other words, the implementation of randomly sampling the CMF yielded a too large scattering of M_core^max to be consistent with the observed values.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Alternative dust temperature estimation methods for massive cores (Method One: 70 um internal luminosity scaling; Method Three: uniform 100 K for all cores) — tested and rejected in favor of Method Two (100 K, with 300 K for W51-E, W51-IRS2, and G327.29) because Methods One and Three gave unrealistically large M_core^max (> 10^3 M_sun) for a few sources and larger scatter.

evidence.quote: We adopted the method two as the fiducial one, since the other two methods led to unrealistically large M_core^max (e.g., >10^3 M_⊙) for a few sources (Table 3).

evidence.loc: C. TEMPERATURE ESTIMATION OF CORES WITHIN MASSIVE CLOUDS
evidence.quote: Method two is adopted in Figure 2 for its least data scatter.

limitations_admitted.value: Hydrogen radio recombination lines (H41alpha) used to subtract free-free emission in ALMA-IMF 1.3 mm images may have maser effects in some regions.

evidence.quote: A caveat is that the hydrogen radio recombination lines may have maser effect in some regions

limitations_admitted.value: Four ALMA-IMF fields (G327.29, G328.25, G351.77, and G353.41) have insufficient (< 5%) short baselines to recover scales larger than 0.1 pc, causing missing flux and potential underestimation of M_core^max.

evidence.loc: 3.3. Mass correlation between most massive core and gravitationally bound gas
evidence.quote: As mentioned by Ginsburg et al. (2022), there are four fields, G327.29, G328.25, G351.77, and G353.41 with insufficient (< 5%) short baselines to recover scales larger than 0.1 pc.

limitations_admitted.value: The spatial resolution used (0.03 pc) is coarser than the native resolutions of ALMA-IMF and HGBS, so extracted 'cores' (radii 0.04–0.23 pc, median 0.1 pc) are larger than cores defined at <= 0.01 pc in recent high-resolution ALMA studies.

evidence.quote: We note that the spatial resolutions we are using are coarser than the native resolutions in the ALMA-IMF and HGBS data.

limitations_admitted.value: Why the theoretical galactic-scale SFR-m_star^max relation from Yan et al. (2017) is applicable on the spatial scale of individual molecular clouds is not yet understood and could be a coincidence.

evidence.loc: 4.1. Connection to the star formation relation
evidence.quote: It is intriguing to see that it is also applicable on the spatial scale of molecular clouds. We do not yet have a good explanation for it.

referee_caveats_inferred: Core masses for nearby clouds are derived by summing Herschel N_H2 maps (fitted from 70–500 um SEDs), whereas distant cloud core masses are derived from single-band 1.3 mm ALMA continuum flux assuming fixed temperatures (100 K or 300 K); systematic differences between these two mass-derivation methods could artificially steepen or flatten the combined M_core^max-M_gas^bound slope.

At 0.03 pc resolution (deconvolved radii up to 0.23 pc), the extracted structures in distant massive clouds are clump/sub-clump halos that fragment into multiple cores at native 2000 AU resolution, Challenging the assumption that a single 0.03 pc structure forms a single most massive star with a 30% efficiency.
Key justification for substituting M_gas^bound for M_gas^dense (HCN luminosity) relies on a companion paper ('Jiao et al. submitted') that was not yet published.

reproducibility.score_reason: The paper uses publicly released, fully reduced archival FITS images (ALMA-IMF Dataverse and HGBS/Hi-GAL archives), states all SExtractor parameters, equations, dust opacities, temperatures, and N-PDF cutoffs in tables, and provides complete output tables for verification. Minor deductions are due to reliance on a custom Orion A map from an earlier paper, unstated cloud boundary definitions for N-PDFs, and details deferred to a submitted companion paper.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: All input ALMA-IMF 1.3 mm free-free subtracted continuum images and Herschel maps are publicly downloadable, the core extraction and mass calculation recipes (smoothing to 0.03 pc, SExtractor settings, gray-body equations, and N-PDF thresholds) are explicitly specified, and the main results (core masses, bound gas masses, and power-law slope 0.506) are numeric and tabulated.
